People keep talking about solar flares, etc as the reason. The real threat would be not flares but CMEs (coronal mass ejections). They are more common during high sun spot activity but can also occur under low sun spot periods. We have been tracking and researching CMEs for decades but predicting them is about as easy as predicting tornadoes. We had two satellites in the 1970s for this purpose and NASA launched STEREO in 2006, which is a more advance CME research satellite. CMEs are so fast, our first warning defense is Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) satellite and that still only gives about 15 minutes up to an hour warning. CMEs can travel from the sun to earth in about 15 hours or sometimes they take days. CMEs (depending on size) can/will increase northern light activity to the point where they can be seen in the lower 48. And yes, they will also fuck with anything electronic. The largest CME recorded was the Carrington CME in 1859, it traveled from the sun to the earth in just a little over 17 hrs. It knocked out all telegraphs in North America and Europe, the Auroras were seen as far south as the Caribbean and were so bright it turned night into day. A Carrington CME today would cost us in the trillions due to the damages it would cause. According to historical data, it would seem we are overdue for another large one, but, since CMEs are unpredictable and when they do occur, we have little warning, so I can't see them shutting down an observatory for that reason.
